acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Users understand how to read discrepancy reports
Users understand how to use the investigation CLI commands
Users understand when to classify findings as BUG vs DESIGN
Users understand how to document investigation rationale
Users understand how to verify bug fixes and mark findings as resolved
Guide includes decision tree for BUG vs DESIGN classification
Guide includes real examples of BUG findings with investigation walkthrough
Guide includes real examples of DESIGN findings with documentation approach

doc.title: Architecture Document
doc.snippet: All findings must be classified as BUG or DESIGN. CLI enforces classification before marking resolved. Unclassified findings block validation completion.

doc.title: Architecture Document
doc.snippet: Finding model: id, layer, description, classification (BUG|DESIGN), rationale, investigated_by, investigated_at, resolved, rustybt_value, backtrader_value.

doc.title: PRD
doc.snippet: FR41-FR54: Present discrepancies, link to source code, track investigation notes, classify as BUG/DESIGN, record rationale, verify fixes, generate regression tests.

doc.title: PRD
doc.snippet: NFR19: Investigation workflow must guide user through classification process. NFR26: All classifications must include timestamps and author.

file.reason: CLI commands for investigation and classification
Data models for findings and discrepancies

constraints.constraint: All findings must be classified as BUG or DESIGN
CLI enforces classification before marking finding as resolved
Findings stored in session/findings.yaml with structured format
Investigation workflow must guide user through classification process (NFR19)
Zero false positives and false negatives in test suite (NFR2, NFR3)
All classifications must include timestamps and author (NFR26)

interface.name: Finding Model
interface.signature: @dataclass Finding: id, layer, description, classification, rationale, investigated_by, investigated_at, resolved

tests.standards: Investigation workflow must guide user through classification process. All classifications must include timestamps and author. Zero false positives and negatives.
